clue.text: It logs the steps of saint touring vault

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the saint's name travels around the vault

parts.note: St Peter, the apostle, gives the name Peter
a dome is a vaulted roof

explanation.surface: A walker's gadget records a visit to a saint's tomb in a church vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' signals the saint's name going round the vault. The definition 'It logs the steps' describes the device rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A step-counting instrument worn while walking records each pace taken.

clue.text: Beating has the boxer's money changing hands

indicators.note: the right hand, R, is swapped for the left hand, L, a change of hands in the letters

parts.note: a boxer fights for a purse, the prize money

explanation.surface: A boxer's prize money passes from one person to another during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in PURSE. 'Beating' looks like the boxing match; it is the noun for a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhythmic throb of the heart in the arteries is its regular beating.

clue.text: Outlaw wantonly speared cheat

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly, without restraint, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: A lawless figure spears someone recklessly and cheats them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wantonly' signals the anagram; 'cheat' looks like part of the surface's misdeeds but supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate bandit of the Wild West living beyond the law is an outlaw.

clue.text: Swallow German beer showing beastly restraint

parts.note: the house martin is a bird of the swallow family
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Swallowing a German beer leads to some animal behaviour being curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb (drink the beer); it is the bird. 'beastly restraint' means a restraint for a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap from girth to noseband stops a horse tossing its head: tack restraining an animal.

clue.text: In Yorkshire the construction worker set off

parts.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens 'the' to t'
a rigger erects scaffolding or rigging on building sites

explanation.surface: A building labourer in Yorkshire sets out for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously clips 'the' to t' (as in 'on t' moor'), giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: To spark off or start an event is to set it going.

clue.text: Describe what may happen when the voting is close

definitions.text: what may happen when the voting is close

explanation.surface: A pundit explains what goes on at a tight election.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate an account is to describe; a second count of ballots follows a narrow result.

clue.text: Charming soldier wears coat, briefly

indicators.note: the soldier wears the coat, so the coat goes around him

parts.note: mac is the short form of mackintosh, a raincoat
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A dashing soldier puts on a short coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' signals the soldier going inside the coat; 'briefly' tells you to use the short name for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enchanting or delightful is described as having a spellbinding quality.

clue.text: Bats surrounding Italian girl

indicators.note: surrounding means the crazy word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: Bats fly around an Italian girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the animals; it is the adjective for crazy. 'surrounding' puts MAD round I.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a young unmarried woman, as in 'maiden'.

clue.text: Egbert endlessly fouled winger

indicators.note: fouled means messed up or tangled, so the letters are jumbled
endlessly means the last letter is cut off the name

parts.note: a man's name, taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer named Egbert keeps committing fouls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the T to leave EGBER, which 'fouled' rearranges. 'winger' looks like a football player; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving waterbird is a creature with wings, a crossword sense of a flier.

clue.text: Accountant has spirit in stock for stew

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: in places the spirit word within the stock word

parts.note: a set is a stock or collection
the soul is a person's spirit

explanation.surface: An accountant keeps spirits in stock for a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests soup stock for the stew; here it means a collection. 'in' signals the spirit going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich French bean dish slow-cooked with meats is a kind of stew.

clue.text: Optical device starts to look at special electronic records

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A gadget looks at special electronic records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of look, at, special, electronic, records.
explanation.definitionFit: A device emitting an intense focused beam of light is an optical instrument.

clue.text: Irritation is a feature found in odd sites

indicators.note: found in means one piece lies inside another
odd means strange, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A skin complaint shows up in strange places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the five letters of 'sites' to ITESS, and 'found in' places the facial feature after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickling urge to scratch is a form of skin irritation.

clue.text: Trip in the dark! Smoothing over is required

explanation.surface: A night out is planned to smooth over a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A night's outing for pleasure is a trip after dark; making something level is smoothing it over.

clue.text: Check blood group for rejection

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
O is one of the blood groups

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a blood group before rejecting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like the definition; it is VET.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ban blocking a proposal is a rejection of it.

clue.text: Barristers sing the French boat song

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
to carol is to sing joyfully
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Lawyers sing a French song about boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' gives LE, the French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian gondolier's song, or music in its rhythm, is a song of boating.

clue.text: Veteran admits great surprise

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the veteran word holds the abbreviation

parts.note: an old stager is a veteran
G is the abbreviation for great

explanation.surface: An old soldier confesses to a big shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like confesses; it puts G inside STAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or amaze someone is to shock them, a sense of surprise.

clue.text: Acolyte having a say in plot

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a site is a plot of land
to tell is to say

explanation.surface: An assistant has a say in a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme; it is a building plot. 'in' signals 'a say' going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or hanger-on who attends a powerful figure is an acolyte.

clue.text: Restraint shown by Turkey having proposition rejected

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the proposition is read backwards

parts.note: a lemma is a proposition in logic or mathematics

explanation.surface: Turkey shows restraint after its proposal is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' signals the logical proposition read backwards, giving AMMEL after Turkey's vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or fetter on free movement is a restraint.

clue.text: Lucia joins MP in reorganisation of the local authority

indicators.note: reorganisation means a rearrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A woman named Lucia teams up with an MP to restructure the council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganisation' rearranges LUCIA, MP and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a town or city council means pertaining to local government.

clue.text: A slattern is overcome when eating a bun

indicators.note: when eating means one word swallows the other

parts.note: to top is to beat or overcome
a roll is a bread bun

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman is overcome while eating a bun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome' looks like part of the slattern's description; it is a verb meaning beat. 'when eating' signals the bun going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a sluttish or untidy woman is a slattern.

clue.text: Tommy's secret

definitions.meaning: Tommy is a British soldier, and 'Tommy's' reads as 'Tommy is'

explanation.surface: A soldier is keeping something to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy (from Tommy Atkins) is a British private soldier; 'Tommy's' is read as 'Tommy is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tommy is a low-ranking British soldier; something confidential is kept from others.

clue.text: Fruit fool commander in Colombia is given

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
CO is the international code for Colombia
a nut is a crazy person, a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish commander in Colombia is given some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the order CO, CO, NUT, not the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hard-shelled tropical palm fruit.

clue.text: Select a strange instrument

indicators.note: strange means unusual, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Choosing an unusual musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges SELECT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument striking metal plates, heard in Tchaikovsky's Sugar Plum Fairy.

clue.text: Live wire

explanation.surface: An energetic person, or an electric cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live wire' reads as an energetic person, but it is two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead a life is to live it in some way; an electric flex is a length of wire.

clue.text: Brooch in silver is creating an impression

indicators.note: in places the brooch word inside the silver word

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pin is a decorative brooch

explanation.surface: A silver brooch makes a striking impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating an impression' looks like making a mark; it means doing an impression of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicking someone imitates them, as an impressionist does.

clue.text: William entertained Heath in English constituency

indicators.note: entertained means hosted, so one name holds the other inside

parts.note: Billy is a pet form of William
erica is the botanical name for heath or heather

explanation.surface: A man named William entertains the politician Edward Heath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' suggests the Conservative prime minister Ted Heath; it is the plant ERICA. BILLERICAY is an Essex town, famous in elections.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Essex that gives its name to a parliamentary seat.

clue.text: The Spanish, in resurgence of handiwork, profit

indicators.note: in places the Spanish article inside the turned word
resurgence means rising again, so the word is turned upwards in this down clue

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home handiwork
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish craftwork is enjoying a revival and making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resurgence of' turns the do-it-yourself abbreviation upwards to YID in this down clue, and 'in' signals the Spanish article going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Return on an investment is its gain or profit.

clue.text: A fish provides food for a culture

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish is served as a meal to a society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'culture' suggests a civilisation; it is a bacterial culture in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaweed jelly on which microbes are grown in the lab.

clue.text: I inform against woman, hence clearing agent

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing on someone to police
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to betraying a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sing' is criminal slang for turning informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatin from fish bladders used to clarify beer and wine is a fining agent.

clue.text: They say drinks deteriorate

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: laps means drinks with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: People claim drinking makes things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' signals that LAPS, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline or slip into a worse state is to deteriorate.

clue.text: The Apostles' writer is of regal disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: The author of a work about the apostles has a kingly character.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apostles is an oratorio by Edward Elgar. 'disposition' looks like temperament; it means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer wrote the oratorio The Apostles (1903).

clue.text: Ale led men astray having glazed appearance

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Beer leads men off the path, leaving them glassy-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges ALE, LED and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Coated with a glossy vitreous finish, like pottery or a fired surface.
